title: Pricing of Climate Risk Insurance: Regulation and Cross-Subsidies
abstract: Homeowners’ insurance, a $15 trillion market by coverage, provides households financial protection from climate losses. Insurance premiums (rates) are subject to significant regulations at a state level in the United States. Using novel data on filings made by insurers to regulators, we propose a metric to quantify the extent of regulation in individual states. We provide evidence of decoupling of insurance rates from their underlying risks and identify regulation as a driving force behind this pattern. Rates are least reflective of risk in states we classify as "high friction", i.e. states where regulations appear most restrictive. We identify two sources behind the decoupling. First, in high friction states, rates have not adequately adjusted in response to the growth in losses. Second, insurers have cross-subsidized high friction states by raising rates in low friction states. Our results imply that households in low friction states are disproportionately bearing the risks of households in high friction states. More broadly, our findings question whether insurance rates can play a useful role in steering climate adaptation and whether households will have continued access to insurance.
abstract_zh: 房主保险按保额计算是一个规模达15万亿美元的市场，为家庭提供抵御气候损失的财务保障。在美国，保险费率（保费）受到各州层面的严格监管。利用保险公司向监管机构提交的新的文件数据，我们提出了一项用于量化各州监管程度的指标。我们提供了证据，表明保险费率与其潜在风险出现了脱钩，并认定监管是造成这一格局的驱动因素。在我们归类为“高摩擦”（即监管看似最为严格的州）的州，保险费率对风险的反映程度最低。我们识别出造成脱钩的两个来源。第一，在高摩擦州，保险费率并未充分地随损失增长而调整。第二，保险公司通过提高低摩擦州的费率，对高摩擦州进行了交叉补贴。我们的结果表明，低摩擦州的家庭不成比例地承担了高摩擦州家庭的风险。更广泛地说，我们的发现对保险费率能否在引导气候适应方面发挥有益作用，以及家庭能否持续获得保险，提出了质疑。

title: Climate Capitalists
abstract: In theory, a cost of capital channel can incentivize green investments like a carbon tax. This channel requires that firms perceive the cost of green capital as lower than that of brown capital. Using hand-collected data, we show that green firms have indeed perceived their cost of capital to be 1 percentage point lower since 2016, when climate concerns by financial investors and governments surged. Moreover, some energy firms have used a lower cost of capital for their green divisions. The findings suggest that the cost of capital can incentivize capital reallocation toward greener investments across firms and within firms.
abstract_zh: 从理论上讲，资本成本渠道可以激励诸如碳税之类的绿色投资。这一渠道要求企业认为绿色资本的成本低于棕色资本。利用手工收集的数据，我们表明，自2016年以来，绿色企业所感知的资本成本确实低了1个百分点，那一年金融投资者和政府的气候关切激增。此外，一些能源企业对其绿色业务部门使用了更低的资本成本。研究结果表明，资本成本可以激励资本在企业之间以及企业内部重新配置，流向更为绿色的投资。

title: Democratizing Private Markets? Private Equity Performance of Individual Investors
abstract: Individual investors match institutional PE performance, but advisor skill and fee layers drive sharp return disparities across households.

title: Limited Risk Transfer Between Investors: A New Benchmark for Macro-Finance Models
abstract: Risk transfer (how much risk changes hands) is small: 0.65% per quarter. Standard models, however, predict 10x more. A new model with inelastic demand provides reconciliation.

title: Rating Without Market Discipline
abstract: We show that private ratings for opaque debt held by life insurers systematically understate credit risk, lower required capital, and reveal the limits of regulation when market discipline is absent.

title: Social Inflation
abstract: I uncover a new source of aggregate risk for the insurance sector: shifts in insurers' loss distribution induced by changing social norms and legal developments.

title: Cross-sectional Skewness
abstract: We evaluate the skewness in the cross-section of returns in light of predictions from a well-known class of asset pricing models.
